lines.li: [them] A traveler at our fire spoke the name of {HOUSE}.
[us] Only a traveler?
[them] Among us, that is how a name begins its walk.
[them] Folk at our market have started saying the name of {HOUSE}.
[us] Kindly, I hope.
[them] Kindly enough, though they still say it quietly.
[them] Your family's name has come up in town once or twice.
[us] Good or bad?
[them] Curious, mostly, people want to know who you are.
[them] Your family's name has turned up on a local channel or two.
[us] Saying what?
[them] Not much yet, just enough to be noticed.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, I am told.
[us] Is that good?
[them] It is a beginning, and at court beginnings are everything.
[them] Every fire in the region knows the name of {HOUSE} now.
[us] That's more fires than I've ever sat at.
[them] A name goes where it is carried, and yours is carried well.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, as our reeve tells it.
[us] The reeve keeps track of such things?
[them] The reeve keeps track of everything, it's the job.
[them] Folks across the region know {HOUSE} by now, I'd say.
[us] For good, I hope.
[them] For good, and that's rarer than you'd think out here.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, by our logs.
[us] You keep logs on us?
[them] We keep logs on everyone, and yours read well.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, no small thing so far from court.
[us] We never sought it.
[them] Honor sought is worth less than honor earned.
[them] Even clans we have never met tell of {HOUSE}.
[us] I've never met them either.
[them] Your name has, and it was welcome there.
[them] Minstrels from far towns sing of {HOUSE} now.
[us] Do they get the names right?
[them] The names, aye, the rest grows with each telling.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, from what I hear on the road.
[us] That's a lot of road.
[them] And a lot of people talking.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, a lot of signal for one family.
[us] We don't send any of it.
[them] Others do, and what they send is good.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, rare for a family with no seat at court.
[us,us:noble] My title came from the Empire, but the name was made out here.
[us] We made it out here, not at court.
[them] Then you have earned your honor twice over.
[them] I don't know {HOUSE}, but every great house started small.
[us] We're not a great house.
[them] Nor were they, once.
[them] Your family's name doesn't ring a bell, I'm afraid.
[us] We're new at this.
[them] Do good work and folks will learn it soon enough.
[them] Your family's name isn't in any record I've seen.
[us] Then we'll have to give the records something to say.
[them] Records fill up fast, given reason.
[them] Forgive me, but {HOUSE} means nothing at court.
[us] We never asked it to.
[them] Spoken like a family that might yet make it mean something.
[them] Traders talk, and your family's name comes up on the road.
[us] Good for business, I hope.
[them] Good for yours, at least.
[them] Before I came here, I was told your family's name is {RENOWN}.
[us] And now that you're here?
[them] I'd say the telling was fair.
[them] So you're one of {HOUSE}, I've heard the name.
[us] Only good things, I hope.
[them] Good enough that I wanted to say hello.
[them] A titled one of a family whose name is {RENOWN}, that is rare.
[us] The title was given, the name was earned.
[them] Both are honor, and you carry both well.
[them] Our hunters say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We've had to defend ourselves.
[them] Then the spirits made you strong for a reason.
[them] Folks on the road say your family's known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We'd rather not need to be.
[them] Nobody would, but it keeps the bandits thinking twice.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, according to people who'd know.
[us] Who's that?
[them] Mercenaries, mostly, and they don't praise lightly.
[them] Our herb-wife says your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We tend whoever needs it.
[them] Aye, and she'd like to trade remedies with you one day.
[them] Our medics say your family's known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Good to hear it from people who'd know.
[them] They'd know, and they don't say it of many.
[them] A family known for {KNOWNFOR} does honor to its name, title or no.
[us] We tend the sick because they need it.
[them] Which is the most honorable reason there is.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and a guest remembers that.
[us,lowtech] There's always room at our fire.
[us] There's always room for a guest here.
[them] Then I will sit, and gladly.
[them] Travelers on the high road say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We like a full table.
[them] So do travelers, which is why they talk.
[them] Your family has a reputation for {KNOWNFOR}, I've heard.
[us] Then let us live up to it.
[them] You already are.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, which at court is a kind of honor.
[us] Out here it's just how we live.
[them] Then you live honorably without trying.
[them] Our traders say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We try to give a fair exchange.
[them] That is why they speak of you.
[them] Merchants at our market say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] And what do they say about our prices?
[them] That they're fair, which is the most a merchant will admit.
[them] Even the Empire's factors say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Trade is trade, whoever it's with.
[them] Spoken like a family that keeps its contracts.
[them] Our crafters say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Hands are for making things.
[them] And yours make them well.
[them] The guild in our town has heard your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Do they want to compete?
[them] They want to see it, and maybe learn a thing or two.
[them] Your family has a name for {KNOWNFOR}, I'm told.
[us] We like things that last.
[them] So do the people who buy them.
[them] A family known for {KNOWNFOR} would find patrons at court.
[us] We make things for our own use, mostly.
[them] The best work usually starts that way.
[them] Our elders say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We hold to what we believe.
[them] The spirits notice those who hold on.
[them] Even our priest has heard your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us,samefaith] Then your priest and I pray alike.
[us] We keep our faith, that's all.
[them] It's more than most do, the priest would say.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, which is rare these days.
[us] Faith keeps us steady.
[them] Out here, steady is worth a lot.
[them] A family known for {KNOWNFOR} is respected at court, whatever its faith.
[us] We don't keep it for respect.
[them] Which is exactly why it earns some.
[them] People at home still talk of your colony's feast.
[us] It was a good day.
[them] And they say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, which fits.
[them] We remember that your colony tended our wounded.
[us] We'd do it again.
[them] I believe it, your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, after all.
[them] Our traders still speak well of dealing with your colony.
[us] We try to be fair.
[them] Your family especially, known for {KNOWNFOR} as it is.
[them] Your colony's fighters came when we called.
[us] A promise is a promise.
[them] And a family known for {KNOWNFOR} keeps it, I hear.
[them] The elders frown when the name of {HOUSE} is spoken.
[us] The elders don't know us.
[them] They know what is told, and that is enough for them.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, I'm sorry to say.
[us] Names can change.
[them] Aye, but it takes longer than it took to spoil them.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, just so you know.
[us] I didn't know.
[them] Now you do, and what you do with it is up to you.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, I regret to say.
[us] Then it's lucky we're not at court.
[them] Honor lost is slow to return, wherever one stands.
[us] What does your family's name count for in your town?
[them] Enough that people expect things of whoever carries it.
[us] And what do they expect of you?
[them] That I keep it up, mostly.
[us] Does your family's name mean much where you're from?
[them] Enough that I'm careful what I put it to.
[us] That sounds like a lot to live up to.
[them] It is, and that is the point of a name.
[us] What does it mean to head a house in the Empire?
[them] It means one's honor is never one's own alone.
[us] That sounds heavy.
[them] It is, and it is worth carrying.
[them] You're one of {HOUSE}, I'm told, and I head {THEIRHOUSE}.
[us] Two families, then.
[them] Two families who would do well to know each other.
[them] I head {THEIRHOUSE}, for what that's worth to a stranger.
[us] My own family name isn't one anyone knows.
[them] Every family's name was unknown once, mine too.
[us] Even out here, people speak of {THEIRHOUSE} with respect.
[them] Honor travels further than any of us do.
[us] Then yours has traveled well.
[us] We've heard the name of {THEIRHOUSE}, even at our colony.
[them,their:tribal] Then the telling has walked far, and I must live up to it.
[them] Then the tale has traveled far, and I must live up to it.
[them] There's a grudge between us and your colony that hasn't been settled.
[us] Then let's not add to it today.
[them] Fair enough, today.
[them] My people keep count of what your colony owes them, and the count is open.
[us] Is it your count or theirs?
[them] Theirs, and mine while I am one of them.
[them] I'll talk, but my people haven't forgotten what lies between us.
[us] Nor have we.
[them] My house has not forgotten its grudge against your colony.
[us] We haven't forgotten it either.
[them] Then we'll speak plainly, and no more than we must.
[them] My house's honor is not yet satisfied where your colony is concerned.
[us] What would satisfy it?
[them] That is not a question for a conversation in passing.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and a family known for {KNOWNFOR} is a good thought in lean times.
[us] Our door's open if anyone needs a meal.
[them] {THEN} is over now, I'm glad to say.
[us] That's good to hear.
[them] Now people have time to talk of other things, your family among them.
[us] Is {THEN} still on at home?
[them] Still, and a family known for {KNOWNFOR} is a warm thought on cold nights.
[us] Come and warm up with us, then.
[us] Is {THEN} on the mend?
[them] Back on their feet, I'm glad to say.
[us] Good, and if it comes back, bring them here.
[them] I would, your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, after all.
[us] Does {THEN} still lead your people?
[them] Still, and {THEN} has heard of {HOUSE} by now.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Good enough, from what I hear.
[them] Our town has a new head now, {NOW}.
[us] Has {NOW} heard of us?
[them] Of {HOUSE}, yes, and not kindly, I'm afraid.
[us] It's been a while since we spoke of trade.
[them] It has, and our traders still ask after a family known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Then send them our way.
[them] We spoke of work last time, and I've thought of your family's {KNOWNFOR} since.
[us] Come and see it whenever you like.
[them] I'll hold you to that.
[them] I've thought about our talk of faith, and that your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Faith is easier with others beside you.
[them] It is, and I'm glad to have met yours.
[us] How is your family keeping?
[them] Well, and they'd like to hear I met one of {HOUSE} out here.
[us] Now you can say you have.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and some at home say a family like yours would know what to do.
[us] I wish we did.
[them] The war with {THEN} is over at last.
[us] I'm glad to hear it.
[them] Peace gives people time to listen, and they ask for news of your family.
[them] {NOW} heads our town now, in place of {THEN}.
[us] Does {NOW} know of us?
[them] A little, your family's name has started to get around.
